observations.seen: A warm dusk glow sits at the far end of the street, but the foreground is lit flat. The player vehicle's rear reads almost pure black, with no sun-driven key or rim light. A single headlight-like hotspot on the road behind the car looks disconnected from any source.
There are no clear cast shadows from the vehicle, cable car, trees or buildings onto the asphalt. Contact grounding under the player car is weak, so objects float.
The dark glossy rear of the player cab shows no environment reflection of the street or sky. Building windows are flat textures with no reflection response.

The San Francisco-style street has brick facades, a cable car, wires, lane markings and street trees, and reads as a coherent place. Buildings repeat a single window texture, and the left curb and sidewalk are sparse.
Mild distance haze appears toward the horizon. There is no visible depth fog between 30 and 180 m to separate building layers, and no light shafts despite the low sun direction.

Brick and window textures look low-resolution and tiled. The player car body is a near-black, undifferentiated material with a noisy, speckled texture. The asphalt is uniform with no roughness variation.
The cable car is reasonably detailed. The player pod vehicle is a simple rounded box with flat red tail-light rectangles. Buildings are extruded boxes with texture-only detail.
The player vehicle takes about 25–30% of the frame and is offset right, so it blocks the road ahead. A large central fare panel and stacked rival name tags clutter the vanishing point.
The chase cam sits low behind the vehicle with a moderate FOV close to 60. The horizon is level and the framing is serviceable, but the camera sits too close for the road to read clearly.
No visible bloom on the tail lights or sun, no film grade, vignette or grain. The image looks close to untonemapped and lacks the burnt-orange/charcoal cinematic grade.

The panels are clean and consistent, with a good speedometer, minimap and fare card. There are too many simultaneous panels, and the center-top fare card plus the bottom debug-like toggles cover large play areas.
